exposure: gallstone intervention during pregnancy (cholecystectomy, ERCP, or combined)
cohort: Pregnant patients aged 18-45 years identified from the Swedish National Register for Gallstone Surgery and Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography (GallRiks) 2009-2016, matched 1:5 with a control group without gallstone intervention during pregnancy.
finding: Gallstone intervention during pregnancy was associated with a higher rate of caesarean section and a shorter duration of pregnancy, including an increased risk of preterm births, but did not affect the newborn child's birth weight (corrected for gestational age) or APGAR score.
mod_finding: Elective caesarean section was more common in the group undergoing gallstone intervention during pregnancy (13.2% vs. 9.0%, p = .034).
birth_weight: Measured as an outcome for newborns, with no significant difference found between intervention and control groups.
gest_age: Measured as an outcome for newborns; shorter duration of pregnancy and more preterm births were observed in the intervention group.
